turnaround_reason: Customer-experience (CX/BPO) outsourcer down ~60% on fears AI is destroying the call-center model, compounded by heavy leverage from the Webhelp acquisition; now statistically the cheapest it has ever been.
bullish_points: Extreme valuation: ~0.16x sales (all-time low), forward P/E ~2.4, EV/EBITDA ~4-5.5x, and ~35% FCF-to-equity yield; FCF $776M vs $1.76B market cap
Q2 EPS $0.91 (net income +38% y/y) and management cites an AI-deal surge — some evidence it can sell AI rather than only be disrupted by it
Momentum turning: +11.7% over 30 days, +7.8% over 5 days; CEO made open-market buys
bearish_points: Existential AI-disruption thesis — the core BPO business may be in secular decline, not just cyclical
Heavy leverage: $5.5B debt, debt/equity 204 — amplifies any revenue erosion
Groupe Bruxelles Lambert sold 6M shares in April; short interest ~18% of float
Guidance implies only ~0.25-1.25% constant-currency growth — barely stabilizing
catalyst: Q3 earnings — a hard near-term print that will test AI-erosion vs stabilization
suggested_trade: Speculative small spot into the Sep 29 print; size for a binary outcome. Not a core hold until AI-erosion is disproven
key_risk: AI genuinely compresses BPO volumes so revenue and FCF erode faster than the company can pay down debt
would_skip_if: Sep 29 print shows accelerating revenue decline or a guidance cut
